timing: Exploratory follow-up after wave one demonstrated better forecast accuracy but worse delivered score on concentric circles. Freeze this analysis before inspecting its new matched pairs or any final-panel outer scores. It cannot change the prospective study, its candidates or its rollout.
question: When two methods were both feasible and later actually measured on the same primary training rows, can training feedback improve the ordering of those two experiments?
training: Only the six historical original incumbent traces used in the lineage protocol. One observation per distinct task and unordered method pair, at the earliest decision with at least one completed primary score and both future candidates still eligible. Each pair member needs a later measured primary result, optionally the preserved stop challenger's primary check. Use only decision-time evidence for features. Ignore exact outcome ties for training and scoring.
method: Use differences between two methods' decision-time novelty, original expected score, generic fit prior, and novelty times the largest previous primary train-to-search score gap (clamp gap to [0,1]). Fit one task-balanced ridge update to predict residual of the two actual later primary score difference minus their current utility difference. Ridge penalty 1, no intercept. Bound each candidate adjustment to +/-0.10, apply to its original utility. Fit once; hold it fixed.
comparisons: Grade each historical fitted task separately from six development incumbent paths and three final root paths. Never use outer labels or other arms. Compare base ordering and revised ordering to the observed sign; a tied guess scores 0.5. Report tasks, pairs, corrections, new errors and unchanged, with separate wave and final sums. Only a higher score on both new groups and at least two final tasks with changed predictions supports further live testing; insufficient support remains inconclusive.
limits: Observed method pairs are selected by the historical planner and overlap within a task. This diagnostic cannot measure the value of stopping or the outcome of an untried method. It makes zero new classifier fits and zero model API requests; the four-coefficient ridge fit is a planning-policy update.
